name: Fix audit findings from the PR #5–#15 review pass (24 findings, 2 critical)
description:
## Context

Independent audit of the PR #5–#15 stack (phase-2c → phase-2.1m), 4 reviewers per PR across isolated
worktrees, every finding adversarially verified before being posted. **24 confirmed findings across
11 PRs** (2 Critical, 18 Major, 4 Minor); 1 raised finding was refuted and dropped. All findings are
already posted as inline review comments on the originating PRs — this issue is the single place to
track fixing them so the PRs themselves can merge without waiting on a fix pass.

Audit summary: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/5bd4c44a-b839-45b4-8fc3-fc9f40b39550

Each item below links to its inline comment thread on the PR for full detail (repro steps, code
pointers). Check items off as they're fixed; fixes should land as new commits on `develop` (or
wherever the code lives once each PR is merged), not by editing the closed PR branches.

## Findings

### PR #5 — Build: stylesheets and markups
- [ ] **Major (docs/correctness)** — `runner.ts` doc comment claims a failed build leaves partial
      output in `distDir`; code actually discards the staging dir wholesale and leaves `distDir`
      untouched.
- [ ] **Major (test coverage)** — two of the four ADR 0056 io-error branches (`read-style`,
      `remove-style`) have no test, despite a manual `chmod 0o000` repro existing.

### PR #6 — Build proofs and `validate` reconciliation
- [ ] **Major (correctness)** — stylelint's "approximate" diagnostic message claims no compiled CSS
      exists even when findings survive dedup for other reasons (stale artifacts, orphaned sheets,
      nested-LESS noise).
- [ ] **Major (robustness/silent failure)** — identity-based dedup can cross-suppress violations from
      an orphaned stylesheet when its selector text collides with a compiled sibling's. Reproduced:
      two same-slot files with identical selectors yield 1 finding instead of 2.

### PR #7 — Dev-engine foundation
- [ ] **Minor (conventions/docs)** — claims `marker.ts` moved "verbatim"; it was actually refactored
      (~61% similarity) and gained a new `RangeError` guard.
- [ ] **Minor (test location)** — a cross-cutting registry test lives under `src/commands/` instead
      of `test/`, against the repo's stated test-location policy.

### PR #8 — The real proxy and the real splice
- [ ] **Critical (robustness)** — `proxyRes` handler has no catch-all; a synchronous throw in the
      passthrough branch (e.g. an invalid header value) becomes an unhandled rejection that hangs the
      request and can crash the proxy silently.
- [ ] **Major (correctness)** — CSP nonce is injected into headers even when the body splice never
      happens, silently tightening the upstream policy and blocking legitimate inline scripts.
- [ ] **Major (robustness)** — the chunk-boundary scan treats literal page text as structural markers
      (e.g. `/common-footer/`, `/order-confirmed/` patterns); real content can silently truncate a
      selective removal.
- [ ] **Minor (docs)** — the coverage-floor file count in `doc/testing.md` is stale for this PR
      (states 6, should be 14).

### PR #9 — Compile and reload
- [ ] **Major (correctness)** — `serveDevModule` strips the entire query string instead of just the
      dev token, breaking Vite's documented resource-query patterns (`?raw`, `?url`, `?worker`).
- [ ] **Major (test coverage)** — per-request compile-error isolation via `AsyncLocalStorage` is never
      tested under real concurrency; a regression collapsing it to shared state would pass every test.
- [ ] **Major (robustness)** — `wireStaleEntriesWatcher` callbacks have no try/catch; an exception
      becomes an unhandled rejection that terminates the process (reproduced with a minimal repro).

### PR #10 — The honesty layer
- [ ] **Major (test coverage)** — the new `runId` validation guard (rejects unescaped `<`/`>` in
      HTML) is never exercised; every test site passes the literal `"test-run"`.

### PR #11 — Dev's overlay and selective removal
- [ ] **Critical (robustness)** — inline watcher wiring dropped the O4 crash guard added in PR #9;
      the new `collectTopLevelStyleModules` call can crash the dev server silently on file save, and
      the exported helper's own O4 tests no longer cover the production code path.
- [ ] **Major (correctness)** — the production-shop warning is skipped when no dev-shop target
      resolves at all, contradicting ADR 0050's amended guarantee.
- [ ] **Major (test coverage)** — the SSE channel callback wiring (`onBuildError`/`onBuildOk`) is
      never tested end-to-end; swapping the two callbacks would pass every test.
- [ ] **Minor (test coverage)** — the new file-append logging utility (`createNodeAppendLog`) ships
      with zero tests; dropping `{ recursive: true }` would go undetected.

### PR #12 — `shoptet init` writes `dist/` into `.gitignore`
- [ ] **Major (conventions/versioning)** — ADR 0007 was amended but its body text is stale: still
      describes appending a single `.shoptet/` line, when it now appends from a list with
      negation-skip logic.

### PR #13 — `validate` colours diagnostics, `NO_COLOR`
- [ ] **Major (conventions/versioning)** — the changeset classifies a required-member addition
      (`colors: OutputColors`) to the published `Output` interface as minor; `doc/versioning.md`'s
      major-bump rule covers narrowing exported types, and the minor carve-out only covers optional
      additions.
- [ ] **Major (test coverage)** — colour wiring from `Output` to `formatDiagnostic` is never tested
      with colour enabled; hardcoding colours to disabled would pass the suite.

### PR #14 — Vendor the review tooling
- [ ] **Major (robustness)** — the vendored plugin trees are protected from Prettier but not from a
      plain Edit/Write; `protect-generated.mjs` wasn't extended to cover them, so nothing warns
      against a hand-edit and `diff -rq` is the only way to detect one.

### PR #15 — Stricli → oclif port
- [ ] **Minor (conventions/docs)** — `doc/configuration.md` still documents the deleted
      `StricliProcess` seam; six other docs were updated for the rename but this one was missed.

## Not in scope here

This issue tracks the audit findings only. It does not track or block the PR stack's merge into
`develop` — that proceeds independently once each PR has the required approval.
